blockers.what_failed: The fuel=0 base case of the induction is unprovable with the current invariant. When fuel=0, classicalExpandBranches returns .openBranch b where b is the first non-closed branch in the list. The invariant says (for sf in expandedSets[j]) Hintikka_rule(sf, b), but does NOT cover sf in b \ expandedSets[j]. These uncovered formulas could violate the Hintikka condition.
what_was_tried: Induction on fuel with the current invariant (∀ i b e, branches[i]? = some b → expandedSets[i]? = some e → ∀ sf ∈ e, ...) — fuel=0 base case fails.
Strengthening the invariant with a saturation precondition (∀ sf ∈ b, sf ∈ e ∨ notApplicable) — fails at call site (branches=[[F(φ)]], expandedSets=[[]], F(φ) is typically applicable and not in []).
Adding (fuel = 0 → ∀ open b' ∈ branches, classicalHintikkaSet b') — not maintained in IH application to new branches after expansion step.
lean_multi_attempt on the fuel=0 case — reached same stuck state at the Hintikka condition for uncovered formulas.
blockers.why_stuck: The algorithm can reach fuel=0 with unexpanded formulas on open branches. The stated invariant only covers ALREADY-EXPANDED formulas (sf ∈ expandedSets[i]). For sf ∈ branches[i] but NOT in expandedSets[i], nothing in the current invariant tells us whether Hintikka_rule(sf, branches[i]) holds. This is a genuine proof gap requiring either a fuel-sufficiency argument or a different induction measure.
blockers.what_is_needed: ONE of: (A) Prove a separate fuel-sufficiency lemma showing that with fuel = 4*(φ.complexity+1)+1, the algorithm NEVER terminates via the fuel=0 degenerate path — i.e., processNext always finds saturation before fuel runs out. OR (B) Restate classicalExpandBranches_hintikka using well-founded recursion on the total number of unexpanded applicable formulas instead of fuel. OR (C) Prove the lemma directly for classicalTableau_hintikka without using classicalExpandBranches_hintikka as an intermediate general lemma.
blockers.fuel_zero_case_in_detail: The fuel=0 case of the induction requires: given (branches, expandedSets) with the invariant, classicalExpandBranches branches expandedSets 0 = .openBranch b → classicalHintikkaSet b. The algorithm at fuel=0 runs `branches.findSome? (fun b' => if isClassicallyClosed b' then none else some b')` and returns the first non-closed branch b. We get isClassicallyClosed b = false (condition 1 of Hintikka). But for condition 2 (∀ sf ∈ b, Hintikka_rule(sf, b)), we can only access Hintikka_rule(sf, b) for sf ∈ expandedSets[j] from the invariant. For sf ∈ b \ expandedSets[j], there is no information. In the actual execution with the correct fuel bound, this case never arises because all applicable formulas get expanded before fuel runs out. But the INDUCTIVE PROOF cannot express this without the fuel-sufficiency lemma.
